page.title: Ruud Hendrikx, creative technologist and physicist
page.description: Ruud Hendrikx, creative technologist and physicist, builds AI agents, machine learning and simulations, at the meeting point of science, philosophy and art. Walk into his workroom, live in the browser.
page.share: Simulations, machine learning and AI agents, made visible. Walk into his workroom, live in the browser. Available for projects.
page.name: Ruud Hendrikx
page.tagline: Creative technologist and physicist. Builds AI agents, machine learning and simulations, at the meeting point of science, philosophy and art
page.offer: Creative technologist and physicist. He builds AI agents, machine learning models and simulations, and makes them something you can see and use. The agents go in close and fast; he keeps the whole in view and decides where they go.
page.ask: Available for freelance projects, hands-on or as technical lead.

work.title: Passenger flow at Schiphol
work.text: For Schiphol he architected and led the simulation of the airport’s operations: passengers through the terminal, the queues, the runways. Before that, a live digital twin of a steel plant for Danieli Corus. He models a system until the people who run it can ask it “what if”.

work.title: LLM assistants in production
work.text: For Schiphol he designed customer assistants on large language models, and is building them into one multi-tenant stack for the airport. At Eneco, the first fully automated pipeline from recorded customer calls to the topics in them. What he builds for is the day after the demo: something an organisation runs every day.

work.title: Models that act early
work.text: At ING he led a data science chapter in Collections and delivered the likelihood-to-pay and early-intervention models. Before that, at Wärtsilä, he turned a market-prediction proof of concept into a client-ready Python package with a production pipeline, and at PGGM he led the early build-out of one of its first data science teams.

own.title: Agentic SWE Atlas
own.text: One run of 46 agents turned the writing of 102 people on building software with agents into one clickable atlas, in 28 minutes: 157 cards, 651 claims. He set the questions and checked the answer: of 2,144 citations, 8 are unresolved.

own.title: Local inference on the 3090
own.text: A coding agent that runs on his own desk. A 27-billion-parameter model on one 24 GB card, driving an agent harness, measured before it was trusted: 43 tokens a second at 55K context, fast enough to work with. Speculative decoding bought the last 44% (30.0 to 43.2). Without it the card holds 144K tokens of context, at 23.2 GiB.

own.title: Metal visuals
own.text: His live visuals engine: Python computes, Swift and Metal draw, values over UDP in between, never pixels. The successor to his Quartz Composer work, for a screen or an LED wall: 256 squares at about 120 fps.

nojs.title: Commodore 64
nojs.text: His first programs, in BASIC. The room you are looking at is a program too: Python driving Blender, one module per object.

nojs.title: TI-83
nojs.text: The graphing calculator he learned to program on, one 96 × 64 pixel screen at a time.

nojs.title: Quantum eraser, classical version
nojs.text: Crossed polarizers on the two slits mark the path, so no fringes. Drop the polarizer into the beam at 45° and they come back. The quantum version needs entangled photons; this one is plain polarization optics. His 2D spectroscopy paper

nojs.title: Cloud chamber
nojs.text: Dry ice, isopropanol, a cold black plate. At sea level a cosmic-ray muon crosses each square centimetre about once a minute, several a second through this plate. The vapour shows the ones it catches: steep ones as short stubs, shallow ones as long lines, the odd fat alpha and a curling beta. The flux is real, the tracks are simulated.

nojs.title: Geiger counter
nojs.text: An SBM-20 tube at background: about 20 counts a minute, Poisson-timed. The rate is real, the counts are simulated. Flip the toggle to hear it.

nojs.title: Oscilloscope
nojs.text: Its probe is hooked onto the Geiger counter’s test point. Each count is one 0.5 ms sweep at 50 µs/div: a negative spike that recovers in ~50 µs, a P31 glow gone in ~50 ms. One instrument reads the other.

nojs.title: Lab notebook
nojs.text: Every line ends in one of three labels: tested, preference, hypothesis. Two 12 V adapters on a handheld scope, on battery, no load: 8 to 13 mV peak to peak, the stock one a little lower. Tested. A fault that felt intermittent happened on every cold open after an album ran out; the gap was in what he had watched.

nojs.title: Structured light, then projection mapping
nojs.text: Gray-code stripes label every point on a plaster head of Plato with a projector column and row; a camera beside the lens triangulates the depth. The head becomes its own point cloud, then a canvas for light.

nojs.title: Luxman L-308
nojs.text: His own amplifier, the last box in a chain he can name from library to cone: Roon holds the files, HQPlayer upsamples them to DSD256, a streamer hands them to the NEO iDSD 2, the Luxman drives the B&Ws. The real one has no meters, so neither does this one.

nojs.title: The records
nojs.text: The library end of the chain. Know a chain well enough and you stop hearing it; then there is only the music.

nojs.title: Disk drive and the disk box
nojs.text: His working life on twelve disks, oldest at the back: physics first, then data science, then agents. The C64 reads the disks through the drive's slot. Type LOAD"$",8 and then LIST.

nojs.title: Disk 1 of 12, UVA.PHYS+PHIL
nojs.text: University of Amsterdam ’07-’11; BSc Bèta-gamma; Major physics, minor philosophy / Aristotle Award ’08: best interdisciplinary research

nojs.title: Disk 2 of 12, UVA.MSC.PHYSICS
nojs.text: University of Amsterdam ’12-’14; MSc Physics; Track: Advanced Matter and Energy Physics

nojs.title: Disk 3 of 12, AMOLF.OPTOMECH
nojs.text: AMOLF ’13-’14; Physics researcher, optomechanics / Built the software for real-time signal acquisition and analysis in light-matter experiments. Automated a nanophotonic optomechanical setup for quantum-state control. / Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 203904 (’15); editorial highlight Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 203904

nojs.title: Disk 4 of 12, VU.2DES
nojs.text: Vrije Universiteit / Laserlab; Amsterdam ’14-’16; Physics researcher, 2D electronic spectroscopy / Designed the software platform of a 2D electronic spectroscopy setup: calibration, signal optimisation, global analysis. Quantum effects in photosynthetic systems. / Sci. Rep. 6 (’16) - JACS (’16); University Research Fellow ’15-’16 Scientific Reports 6 JACS

nojs.title: Disk 5 of 12, PGGM.DATASCI
nojs.text: PGGM ’16-’17; Data science consultant / Early build-out of one of PGGM’s first data-science teams. Prototypes: call-centre forecasting, fraud and bankruptcy risk, client profiling, micro-targeted marketing.

nojs.title: Disk 6 of 12, WARTSILA.ML
nojs.text: Wärtsilä ’18; Machine learning engineer / A reusable market-prediction ML solution: from proof of concept to a client-ready Python package with a production-ready ML pipeline.

nojs.title: Disk 7 of 12, TELE2.VOICE
nojs.text: Tele2 ’18-’19; Lead data scientist / End-to-end 4G voice-quality analytics on call detail records: performance monitoring, root-cause analysis, degradation modelling.

nojs.title: Disk 8 of 12, ING.COLLECTIONS
nojs.text: ING ’19-’21; Chapter lead data science / Machine learning to scale collections operations, leading a data science / analytics chapter. Likelihood-to-pay and early-intervention prevention models.

nojs.title: Disk 9 of 12, SCHIPHOL.SIM
nojs.text: Royal Schiphol Group ’21-’23; Senior data scientist / Airport operational simulation and forecasting: passenger departure flow, queue lengths, waiting time, demand and capacity prediction, runway capacity modelling. / The case: LOAD"SIMULATIONS",8

nojs.title: Disk 10 of 12, STEEL.TWIN
nojs.text: Danieli Corus ’23; Technical lead, steel plant simulation / A modular, real-time digital twin of a steel plant for what-if simulations: capacity planning and scheduling. A digital-shadow tool for bottleneck detection.

nojs.title: Disk 11 of 12, ENECO.SQUAD
nojs.text: Eneco ’23-’25; Lead data scientist / Built the company’s first data science squad. The first fully automated topic-modelling pipeline for CX: voice transcription at scale, embedding, clustering, summarisation.

nojs.title: Disk 12 of 12, SCHIPHOL.LLM
nojs.text: Schiphol ’25; AI solution engineer / LLM-powered CX assistants on Azure OpenAI Service. A modular framework on LangChain, LangGraph, Redis memory and FastAPI: intent classification, hybrid RAG, agentic tool use. Multi-tenant. / The case: LOAD"AGENTS",8

nojs.title: The small PC
nojs.text: His own build: a small case with the graphics card standing behind its open side. The local models run here.

nojs.title: Pads and faders
nojs.text: What his hands are on when the visuals run.

nojs.title: Mapping kit
nojs.text: A small projector and a card model of a house front: where a show for a building starts.

nojs.title: The cabinet
nojs.text: A cabinet of curiosities: things he keeps for what they make him think about.

nojs.title: Planarian, two heads
nojs.text: Michael Levin’s lab briefly disturbed a cut flatworm’s bioelectric signalling, and it regrew with two heads. Cut again, untreated, it grew two heads again.

nojs.title: Möbius band
nojs.text: One side, one edge: inside and outside are one surface.

nojs.title: Light-harvesting complex
nojs.text: Photosynthesis under glass. At the Vrije Universiteit he built the software for a 2D electronic spectroscopy setup that revealed quantum effects in photosynthetic systems: dark states in the light-harvesting complex LH2 (Scientific Reports, 2016).

nojs.title: LED matrix
nojs.text: A grid of squares, each with a live alpha: the core of his Metal visuals engine, the successor to an old Quartz Composer workflow for TVs and LED walls.

nojs.title: Rule 30, row by row
nojs.text: Rule 30, drawn as it is computed: each row from the row above, nothing else. One black cell to start, one row a step since you came in. No formula skips ahead: to see row n, the rows before it have to be drawn. The red lines mark the only past the newest middle cell can depend on.

nojs.title: The books
nojs.text: The books on the cabinet under the window, and one open on the desk: McGilchrist, Abram, Koch, Kastrup, Schopenhauer, Faggin, Hoffman, Bohm, Lane, Feynman, Hawking, Wolfram, Hertog. His definition: consciousness turns raw information into felt, meaningful experience, not reducible to syntax. AI trains on the last, most compressed layer. The map is not the territory.

nojs.title: The shelf
nojs.text: McGilchrist, Abram, Koch, Kastrup, Schopenhauer, Faggin, Hoffman, Bohm, Lane, Feynman, Hawking, Wolfram, Hertog. His definition: consciousness turns raw information into felt, meaningful experience, not reducible to syntax. AI trains on the last, most compressed layer. The map is not the territory.

nojs.title: The principle of least action
nojs.text: Give every path one number, the action S = ∫(T − V) dt. Nature takes the path where small detours don't change it: δS = 0. That single condition gives the Euler–Lagrange equation, and from it F = ma. A Legendre transform, H = pq̇ − L, trades velocity for momentum, and Hamilton's equations follow. Feynman's reason: every path counts, but only near δS = 0 do they add up instead of cancelling. The camera that flew you in rode such a path, like a bead on a wire. After Erik Verlinde's classical mechanics lectures (UvA, c. 2009). A year later he asked where F = ma itself comes from.

nojs.title: A drop on the glass
nojs.text: Watch a drop run down the glass. No one can predict which way it turns next. Science calls that chaos, as if it were out of control. David Abram puts it better: not out of control, only out of ours. Wild.

cards.title: The decks
cards.body: Two decks and a two-channel mixer, a record of his own on each: warm deep house on the left, minimal techno-house on the right. Start either and the facades across the water play along. Start the other while one plays and it comes in on the beat, the crossfader handing over in eight bars. A low cut drops the facade into a breakdown. Both records are synthesised at 122 BPM, rendered offline and fetched at a deck’s first play. Until a record arrives, the browser plays it live.

cards.title: B&W DM603
cards.body: Three-way floorstanders with the yellow Kevlar midrange B&W is known for. Around 90 dB sensitive: an easy load for the Luxman.

cards.title: iFi NEO iDSD 2
cards.body: The DAC. Music reaches it upsampled to DSD256, and the display reads 11M when it locks.

cards.title: Sennheiser HD 660S2
cards.body: Open-back, 300 Ω, driven straight from the NEO iDSD 2. The quiet half of the chain.

cards.title: The shelf
cards.body: McGilchrist, Abram, Koch, Kastrup, Schopenhauer, Faggin, Hoffman, Bohm, Lane, Feynman, Hawking, Wolfram, Hertog. His definition: consciousness turns raw information into felt, meaningful experience, not reducible to syntax. AI trains on the last, most compressed layer. The map is not the territory.

cards.title: Two hemispheres
cards.body: McGilchrist’s claim is not left-logic, right-creativity: both halves do everything, and what differs is the attention. The narrow look takes a thing apart, and it only means something once it is back in the whole; that is how this room moves. Agents are the emissary, brilliant and fast on the most compressed layer. The human stays the master and holds the strategy.
